children: Gujarat Themis Biosyn Limited (GTBL) on Friday said it has completed the acquisition of Japan-based MicroBiopharm Japan Co., Ltd. (MBJ) for ¥21.5 billion (Rs 1,300 crore), giving the Indian fermentation-focused drugmaker access to new technologies, regulated manufacturing facilities and established relationships with global pharmaceutical companies.

The acquisition, first announced on May 22, was completed through GTBL's wholly owned Japanese subsidiary, Themis Biosyn Japan Limited (TBJ), after receiving the regulatory approvals and satisfying other closing conditions.

GTBL said it invested Rs 475 crore as capital contribution and Rs 745 crore as a loan in the Japanese subsidiary Themis Biosyn Japan (TBJ) to fund the acquisition. GTBL has also entered into a loan agreement with TBJ for a facility of up to Rs.800 crore, with the proceeds intended for the acquisition.

Avendus Capital arranged the full acquisition financing through a tailored mix of onshore and offshore debt, addressing the complexities of the cross-border transaction. Avendus Structured Credit Fund III acted as the lead investor in the onshore debt financing.

The transaction brings together Indian capital and Japanese operating assets, enabling GTBL to combine its fermentation capabilities and manufacturing scale with MBJ's more than six decades of pharmaceutical R&D and manufacturing expertise, as well as its established relationships with global pharmaceutical companies.
GTBL looks to build global CDMO business

The acquisition is part of GTBL's plan to evolve from a fermentation-focused pharmaceutical manufacturer into a more broadly integrated global contract development and manufacturing organisation, or CDMO.

MBJ operates three GMP-compliant manufacturing plants and has a track record of inspections by the US Food and Drug Administration and Japan's Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency. It reported revenue of ¥9.5 billion in FY26, with about 40 percent coming from outside Japan. Its six largest customers have been associated with the company for more than two decades.

Importantly, the acquisition takes GTBL into areas beyond its existing fermentation portfolio. MBJ brings a proprietary P450 enzyme platform used for enzyme-based bioconversion, alongside capabilities in plasmid DNA, antibody-drug conjugate conjugation and recombinant proteins. Its portfolio also includes APIs and intermediates used in oncology, immunosuppressants, peptides and antibiotics.

GTBL expects to leverage its lower-cost Indian manufacturing base alongside MBJ's technology and customer relationships to improve cost competitiveness and potentially expand margins on higher-value products. The company also expects the transaction to be earnings-per-share accretive.
MBJ's existing management will continue to run the Japanese operations following the acquisition.

“The successful completion of this acquisition marks a defining milestone in GTBL's journey towards becoming a fermentation-based, globally integrated CDMO,” Dr. Sachin Patel, managing director of Gujarat Themis Biosyn Limited, said.

Deloitte India was the exclusive financial adviser to GTBL, while Tokyo International Law Office (TKI) Japan served as legal counsel. Avendus Capital was the exclusive financing arranger for the transaction.

title: Gujarat Themis completes Rs 1,220-crore funding for Japan acquisition
